_comment: Edit this, not the code. Models are Claude Code aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku) or full model ids. max_cost_usd and worker_budget_usd are the SDK's local token-cost ESTIMATE at API list prices, not money billed on a subscription — useful only as a relative throttle. On a subscription the real limit is your plan's usage cap; max_cycles is the ceiling that matters. on_quota=rotate expects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to point at the OmniRoute gateway: a usage limit then re-issues the call so the gateway serves it from the next account in its pool. Rotation is skipped automatically when the run is pointed straight at Anthropic.
goal:
Finish Phase 2, then build ONE data-source slice. Do not start Phases 4, 5 or 6, and do not attempt the rest of Phase 3 (Moodle REST, work items, time logging, TravelTimeProvider/MapKit, notifications, mail triage, the planner).

A. PARSA'S DEFECT — routine blocks are stuck on Mon/Wed/Fri (highest priority)
Creating an event on any other weekday silently relocates it to Mon, Wed or Fri, and blocks cannot be dragged to another day. Root cause is understood: the mock template is activeWeekdays [2,4,6] and RoutineWeekLayout returns nothing outside that set, so the *filtering* is correct. The defect is that the app does this silently — Parsa could not tell why it was happening.
This needs a DA ruling first, then a CA fix. The question for DA: when a user creates or drags a routine block onto a weekday outside the template's active set, what should happen — add that weekday to the template, refuse with a visible reason, or offer the choice? Also: how is a template's active-weekday set made visible on the canvas so inactive days read as inactive rather than broken? Silent relocation is not an option.

B. FINISH THE SCREENSHOT SET — Parsa asked for this explicitly
screenshots/2 has items 1-3, half of 6, and 8. Capture the rest of components.md §17: items 4 and 5 (detached instances, re-sync popover, the main-grid inspector line), 9 (needs-attention row at 1, at 12, at 0), 10 (status item normal/late/empty, full width and clipped), 11 (popover normal/late/empty and beyond popoverMaxRestRows), 12 (snooze result row, same-day and next-day). Update screenshots/2/INDEX.md. Parsa cannot find several of these features himself, so the captures are how he reviews them.
G-017 (ConflictEngine structurally caps conflicts at 2 options with isRecommended always index 0, so §17 items 6-three-option and 7 cannot occur) needs a DA ruling: relax §17, or fix ConflictEngine to produce 2-3 ranked options per BRIEF-PRODUCT. Decide it; do not leave it open.
Then DA reviews the whole set against the spec, and Phase 2 is done.

C. THE DATA-SOURCE SLICE — WebDAV-hosted ICS, not a public feed
Parsa's real timetable lives on his university's CIS server over WebDAV (host cis.technikum-wien.at, path /Webdav/Lvplan), behind HTTP basic auth, and that directory is expected to contain .ics files. So this slice is: fetch over authenticated WebDAV, parse iCalendar (RFC 5545), import read-only events, poll on a schedule.
Phase 3 has no design coverage — DA must spec this slice before CA builds it, scoped to this one source only.
Hard requirements: credentials go in the macOS Keychain, never in the repo, never in a config file, never in a log, never in a test fixture. No credential is ever committed. Build and test against a local sample .ics file and a mocked WebDAV response — you do not have Parsa's credentials and must not ask for them. Imported events are read-only and clearly attributed to their source.
When the importer is verified against sample data, report PHASE_DONE and stop. Parsa will supply his own credentials to the running app himself.
